name: wavvy 4.0in ILI9488 panel (plain ESP32 WROOM)
summary: The big tier 0 panel: 320x480 portrait on a 4MB no-PSRAM ESP32, which is more pixels than fit in one buffer.

render.reason: 320x480 at 8 bits indexed is 153.6KB in one contiguous block, which the ESP32 will not give you once WiFi is up. So the compositor works in 16-row bands: a 5.1KB indexed band plus a 15.4KB three-byte staging buffer, 20.5KB total instead of 153.6KB, at the cost of walking the draw list once per band. 16 rows is the same block height the proven wavvy video firmware converts with.

display.pixel_format_reason: The ILI9488 has no 16-bit SPI pixel mode. Every pixel is three bytes on the wire, using the top 6 bits of each channel. That is the hard ceiling on frame rate and no amount of clock will move it. It is also why the panel is not an ST7796, which is wired identically and does have a 16-bit mode.
display.clock_reason: Measured. 80MHz is right at the edge of what these modules tolerate and this particular board is stable there. Rebuilding at 40MHz roughly doubled blit time for a 320x192 draw, 53ms to 85ms, which confirms the clock actually takes effect. The remaining ceiling is FIFO refill overhead in the bulk writer, not the clock.

bluetooth_keyboard.reason: No touch and no panel-side buttons, so a BLE keyboard is the only real input. NimBLE at 19KB rather than Bluedroid at 83KB, same as every other no-PSRAM board in the fleet.

touch.absent_reason: Bare panel module wired to a plain ESP32 devkit. There is no touch layer on the glass and no touch controller on either board.

bad_baud_rates.reason: Invalid head of packet (0xFF) on this CP2102 cable, including for plain esptool reads. It is the cable, not the board.
Same Invalid head of packet (0xFF) failure as 921600.

panel_id_register.note: This is the read that killed autodetection for the whole project. 0xD3 should return the controller ID; it returns 00 7F DF, which matches no known part. The panel really is an ILI9488, proven with a labelled test card drawn under each candidate driver, not with a register read.

distinguishing_notes: 4.0 inch panel. That is the only difference from the 3.5in board: same chip, same flash, same controller, same wiring, same clone CP2102 reporting USB serial 0001.
esptool cannot separate the two boards. Measure the glass or read the MAC.
locationID in ioreg -r -c IOUSBHostDevice -l is unique per physical USB port and can tell two identical bridges apart if both are plugged in.
identification.confirm_prompt: Is this the 4.0 inch panel? The 3.5 inch board is electrically identical but is NOT stable at 80MHz. Flashing this profile onto the 3.5in board does not fail, it renders block corruption.

gotchas.text: No 16-bit SPI pixel mode. Three bytes per pixel, always. A full 320x480 frame is 460.8KB on the wire, so anything that assumes RGB565 transport sizing will be off by 50 percent.
230400 only. 921600 and 460800 both fail with Invalid head of packet (0xFF) on this CP2102 cable, including for esptool reads. The flasher must never offer them.

MISO is deliberately left unassigned even though GPIO19 is available. The panel is write-only, and the ESP32 SPI driver refuses to clock above 26.7MHz once a MISO pin is bound, so binding it silently costs two thirds of the clock.
153.6KB of indexed framebuffer will not come back as one contiguous allocation with WiFi up. Band rendering is not an optimisation here, it is the only thing that fits.

Attaching a serial monitor resets the board through DTR/RTS. Anything streaming to it drops for a few seconds and reconnects. A broken pipe in a host-side log exactly when the monitor opened is expected, not a bug.
Both CP2102 bridges in the fleet report USB serial 0001, so with both boards plugged in the /dev/cu.usbserial-* names collide. Flash one at a time, or match on locationID from ioreg.
